_comment: Routing policy. Readable and editable by the support manager; every rule is cited in the decision log by id. Changes take effect on restart. Thresholds were chosen from out-of-fold predictions on the development set - see docs/thresholds.md.

never_auto_intents.reason: This type of request always goes to a person: security and compliance carry contractual and legal risk, and feature or unclear requests have no documented answer.

sensitive_topic_tripwire.reason: The ticket mentions a possible security compromise, a payment dispute or a legal matter. These always go to a person, whatever the classifier thinks the ticket is about (safety net independent of the model).

sensitive_runner_up.reason: The classifier's leading guess is a routine request, but it also gives real weight to a security or compliance reading, so a person should check.

incident_intents.reason: A live, high-urgency performance or database incident needs an engineer looking at the customer's own system, not only a documentation answer.

intent_confidence_threshold.reason: The classifier was not confident enough about what this ticket is asking.

answerable_threshold.reason: The ticket looks unlikely to be answerable from the knowledge base.

retrieval.reason: No documentation passage was relevant enough to ground an answer.

kill_switch.reason: Automatic answering is switched off (kill switch); every ticket goes to a person.
